Figure 1:Beyond Predefined Factories: Rich, Editable Procedural Worlds.InfiniDream extends an existing procedural generator to create novel assets and visually rich 3D scenes.
We compare its results with existing VLM-based
3D scene generation methods.

Figure 2:Motivation: Beyond predefined procedural factories.Given a flowering cactus desert prompt,
VLM-based code generation produces simplified
geometry, predefined factories offer limited
variations, and parameter-based generation
struggles to introduce new features.
InfiniDream extends existing procedural
generators to create novel assets within
rich, photorealistic 3D worlds.

Figure 3:Comparison of procedural asset generation strategies.From left to right: VLM-generated Blender code
from scratch, predefined Infinigen factories,
VLM Agent Harness with full Infinigen access,
and our symbolically constrained editing.

Figure 4:Procedural asset generation through SCE.(A) Factory mapping and retrieval.
(B) Structured editing plan.
(C) Coarse asset construction.
(D) Render-guided fine refinement.
Existing procedural algorithms are reused
under explicit editing constraints.

Figure 5:Overview of InfiniDream’s end-to-end world generation pipeline.(A) Scene Picker collects the user instruction
and current scene information.
(B) Director generates a structured Scene Plan.
(C) Asset Generator creates procedural assets.
(D) Deterministic frustum-guided placement
identifies valid object locations.
(E) Population instantiates diverse assets.
(F) Terrain refinement and rendering
produce the final scene.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison of
object-level generation.Generated 3D assets under identical
text prompts.

Figure 7:From text to richly detailed 3D worlds.Qualitative comparisons across four diverse environments,
highlighting scene richness, visual fidelity, and semantic alignment.
All methods use identical text prompts.

Figure 8:High-quality and diverse procedural assets.InfiniDream generates five variations by changing
random seeds, while TRELLIS.2 uses five independently
generated reference images.

Figure 9:Quantitative object-level ablation.Evaluation of generation components and
refinement strategies across 25 animal and
plant tasks, measuring semantic alignment,
visual similarity, and perceptual quality.

Figure 10:Qualitative object-level ablation.Visual comparison of different generation
strategies, illustrating the effects of
reference images, factory selection,
structured planning, and iterative refinement
on asset geometry, fine-grained details,
and visual appearance.

Table 5:Quantitative scene-level placement ablation.Evaluation on 20 scenes measuring object
readability, ground contact, and contact spread.

Figure 11:Qualitative scene-level placement ablation.Visual comparison of different placement strategies,
illustrating the effects of semantic planning,
grid-based placement, and anchoring constraints
on object visibility, spatial arrangement,
and scene composition.

Figure 12:Additional qualitative comparisons of object-level generation.More examples comparing InfiniDream with existing
methods under identical text prompts.

Figure 13:Additional qualitative comparisons of scene-level generation.More examples of 3D world generation across diverse
environments under identical text prompts.

Figure 14:Additional qualitative comparison with GPT-6 Astra.We compare InfiniDream, implemented with Claude Opus 4.8,
against GPT-6 Astra on representative examples under identical
text prompts. The results provide additional evidence of
InfiniDream’s ability to generate visually rich and
semantically coherent procedural assets and scenes.

Figure 15:Additional qualitative diversity comparisons
with TRELLIS.2.Five variations are generated for each text prompt.
InfiniDream achieves procedural diversity by varying
random seeds, whereas TRELLIS.2 uses independently
generated reference images.
Figure 16:Object-level comparison with Code2Worlds.
Figure 16:Object-level comparison with Code2Worlds.

Figure 17:Qualitative comparison of man-made asset generation.InfiniDream produces structurally coherent
man-made objects with rich geometric and material details.
